clue.text: River to rise — that same river's trapped creature

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: trapped says the second river is held captive inside the word rise

parts.note: taken as written
the Po once more, the river already used at the start

explanation.surface: A river is about to flood, and an animal is caught in its waters.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one river in flood, but 'that same river' asks for Italy's river a second time, and 'trapped' holds that second copy inside the word the clue prints.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small toothed whale related to the dolphin is one kind of animal.

clue.text: Attendants taking time following head of empire joke

indicators.note: following places the time piece after the other two pieces in the answer
the head of a word is its opening letter, here that of empire

parts.note: source of the opening letter
a quip is a witty remark or joke
an age is a long stretch of time

explanation.surface: Courtiers take their cue to laugh after the emperor cracks a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the pieces out of answer order: 'following' sends the word for time to the back, behind the letter from 'head of' and the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an old word for a retinue, the servants and carriages accompanying a grand person.

clue.text: Mum and boy, a quiet little boy socially awkward?

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a lad is a boy
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
Ted is a short form of the boy's name Edward

explanation.surface: A family of three, with the younger son shy and ill at ease in company.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: someone unable to adjust to their surroundings struggles in company, the question mark admitting the looseness.

clue.text: Modify piece of furniture in church according to report

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so the church furniture is heard rather than read

parts.note: the altar is the table at the east end of a church

explanation.surface: Someone wants a pew or lectern adapted, as the parish minutes record.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both verbs mean to change something slightly.

clue.text: Something eaten in lorry — the man's eating all right!

parts.note: an artic is British slang for an articulated lorry, a large truck with a trailer

indicators.note: eating says one piece swallows another, taking it inside

parts.note: the man is he, the apostrophe-s standing for 'is'
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A trucker has a snack in his cab and is tucking in happily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link; the container signal is 'eating', which puts OK inside HE. ARTIC is British shorthand for an articulated lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a globe-shaped vegetable with edible leaf bases and heart is one kind of food.

clue.text: A fresh start for pupils before they were eleven?

definitions.text: A fresh start for pupils before they were eleven?

parts.words: A fresh start for pupils before they were eleven?
parts.note: young schoolchildren once wrote on small boards of grey stone that were wiped at the start of each lesson, so a wiped board was literally their new beginning

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for a fresh start is taken literally: junior-school children, below the age of the old British eleven-plus exam, once wrote on wipeable writing tablets.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the phrase means a new beginning with past mistakes wiped away.

clue.text: Perhaps Oxford's leading element needs to step up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for step is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: The head of a university college, or its top student, must raise their game.
explanation.walkthrough: An Oxford is a style of laced shoe, so its leading element is the front part. 'needs' is a link; 'up' turns PACE into ECAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the reinforced front of a laced shoe is the foremost part of footwear such as this style.

clue.text: Responsibilities of the French with strings attached

parts.note: du is French for 'of the'
ties are strings or cords used for fastening

explanation.surface: France's obligations come with conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both words name tasks one is obliged to carry out.

clue.text: Defeat sees king ousted

parts.note: R is the abbreviation of rex, Latin for king
someone ousted is out, removed from their position

explanation.surface: Losing a battle leads to a monarch being deposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an overwhelming beating that sends the losers fleeing in disorder.

clue.text: Most impressive workshop almost blocking two streets

indicators.note: something blocking a way sits in the middle of it, so the workshop goes between the pair of streets
two tells you the street abbreviation is used twice over

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street

indicators.note: almost means the workshop word falls one letter short, losing its end

parts.note: an atelier is an artist's workshop or studio

explanation.surface: A very grand garage or studio nearly obstructs a pair of roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final R of the French-derived word for a studio, and 'blocking' sets what is left between the pair that 'two streets' supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the superlative of an adjective meaning grand and dignified.

clue.text: Where many of you will now be writing, in theory

definitions.text: Where many of you will now be writing
definitions.meaning: solvers filling in a printed crossword are writing on a sheet of newsprint
something that works only as a written plan, not yet in practice

explanation.surface: A remark to readers about where they are supposedly putting pen at this moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal and idiom: the solver's pen is on newsprint, and the phrase also means hypothetically rather than in practice.

clue.text: Police tense about period long ago

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Officers are still on edge over an era from the distant past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the eleven letters of POLICE and TENSE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the geological epoch of the ice ages, ending about twelve thousand years back.

clue.text: Absurd behaviour of cleaner (a dame, not a maiden)

parts.note: a char is an old British word for a woman hired to clean a house

indicators.note: not tells you the second phrase's letters are absent from the first

parts.note: taken as written
A as written, plus M, the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A cleaning woman of mature years, a titled lady at that, acts ridiculously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes A and M (maiden, from cricket scorecards) from A DAME, leaving ADE. A CHAR is an old British word for a cleaning woman. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a ridiculous pretence or farce, as in 'the trial was a farce'.

clue.text: Thinking outside the box may lead to these inside it!

definitions.text: Thinking outside the box may lead to these inside it!

parts.words: Thinking outside the box may lead to these inside it!
parts.note: an office or shop has a box where people post their ideas for improvements, and original thinking produces such ideas

explanation.walkthrough: The box changes meaning midway: first the idiom for conventional thinking, then the real box in which staff or customers post their ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: proposals for improvement are what people post into such a container at work.

clue.text: Marked with sign of approval or shown disapproval?

definitions.meaning: an item on a list given a check mark to show it is right or done
informally, told sharply that one has behaved badly; scolded

explanation.surface: A piece of school work either gets the teacher's check mark or a frown.
explanation.definitionFit: Two opposed senses: given a check mark as correct, and reprimanded for doing wrong.

clue.text: Many rise when trained in educational establishment

indicators.note: trained things are drilled into shape, so these letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Plenty of people get on in life after being taught at a good college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when trained' rearranges MANY and RISE together; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a college where priests, ministers or rabbis study.

clue.text: Flap during road accident in which animal may have got killed

definitions.text: in which animal may have got killed

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so the flap sits within the accident word

parts.note: a shunt is British slang for a minor car crash, one car running into the back of another
a tag is a small flap or tab attached to something

explanation.surface: Panic at a car crash where a deer or dog may have died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flap' reads as a panic but is a small tab; 'during' sets it within British slang for a rear-end car collision.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the pursuit of male deer with hounds, a chase that may end in the quarry's death.

clue.text: It would be unusual for this spy to be centre stage

indicators.note: unusual means not in the normal form, so the letters take a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An undercover operative is the last person who would want the limelight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges CENTRE STAGE. The whole sentence is also true of the answer, who works out of the limelight.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an undercover operative gathering intelligence covertly for a government.

clue.text: Season to be frugal with article unavailable

indicators.note: unavailable means the article cannot be had, so it is missing from the word

parts.note: sparing means economical, using little
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A time of year for thrift, when a particular item cannot be bought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unavailable' drops the A from SPARING; 'to be' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the three months after winter are one of the four parts of the year.

clue.text: Seize foreign money after initial 80 per cent devaluation

indicators.note: the opening letter, read as a Roman numeral, loses four fifths of its value: five hundred falls to one hundred

parts.note: the dollar is the currency of the USA and other countries, foreign to a British solver
D is the Roman numeral for 500
C is the Roman numeral for 100, a fifth of 500

explanation.surface: Grab overseas currency once it has slumped to a fifth of its worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after initial 80 per cent devaluation' works on Roman numerals: the opening D (500) of DOLLAR drops by four fifths to C (100).
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: informally, to grab or arrest someone, as police do a suspect.

clue.text: Further test limited by broken rope

indicators.note: limited by means bounded by, so the test has the other letters on both sides
something broken is in pieces, so the letters of the next word are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for cars in Britain

explanation.surface: An additional trial is cut short when a cable snaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Further' is a verb here, not 'additional'. 'broken' makes PROE, and 'limited by' sets Britain's yearly roadworthiness check for cars within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: as verbs, both mean to advance or help forward a cause.

clue.text: Listening to explosive, say, wanting noise restricted

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for high explosive

indicators.note: restricted means confined, so the noise is shut inside the letters before it

parts.note: eg means for example, or say
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Someone hears a blast or the like and wishes the racket were kept down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is not speech but 'for example'; 'restricted' confines the racket within it, and 'wanting' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: paying attention to and taking notice of advice or a warning.

clue.text: Husband has upset woman — could it make her go red?

definitions.text: could it make her go red?

parts.note: H is the genealogical abbreviation for husband

indicators.note: in a down clue, something upset is overturned, so the name reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A man has annoyed his wife and wonders whether she will flush with anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ANNE into ENNA; 'has' is a link. Going red is not blushing but colouring the hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a plant dye that tints hair a reddish-brown shade.

clue.text: This writer's sure to make a prediction of personal restriction

definitions.meaning: an old-fashioned expression of certainty, said by the setter in the first person: I am certain of it
taken literally, the speaker forecasts being tied up in future

explanation.surface: The setter confidently forecasts a loss of his own freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' links the two readings: the old-fashioned idiom of certainty, and the same words taken literally as a forecast of being tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom and literal reading: an expression meaning 'I am certain', and a forecast that the speaker will be tied up.

clue.text: A bishop gets in the way of union — it's forbidden

indicators.note: something in the way of another sits in its middle, obstructing it

parts.note: TU is the abbreviation for trade union
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman obstructs a marriage that the church will not allow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets in the way of' puts A and B inside TU, a trade union; 'it's' is a link. The answer is a variant spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: prohibited by social or religious custom.

clue.text: Terrible danger, even in ground-floor apartment

indicators.note: terrible means in a bad state, so the letters of the next word are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
an even surface is flat and level

explanation.surface: There is awful peril even in a home at street level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges DANGER into GARDEN; 'in' is a link. 'even' looks like an adverb of emphasis but means level.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the British term for a home at street level with its own access to a lawn or yard.
